items.name: add-to-cart-button
items.title: Add To Cart Button
items.description: An add-to-cart button whose product thumbnail flies along an arc into a cart icon (via ref or a screen corner), with idle, adding and added states and a companion CartIcon whose badge bumps on each add. Announces the result via aria-live; with reduced motion the flight is skipped and states switch instantly.

whenToUse: Product cards and quick-add rows in a shop
Any action that moves an item somewhere the user can see
watchOut: Point the flight at a cart icon that stays visible, or the motion has nowhere to land
Keep the server request independent of the animation so a slow network does not freeze it

items.name: animated-number
items.title: Animated Number
items.description: An odometer-style number that rolls digit by digit with Intl currency or number formatting and a brief green or red hint plus arrow when the value rises or falls. Use for prices, totals and counters; screen readers get the formatted text, and reduced motion swaps instantly.

whenToUse: Prices, totals and counters that change after a choice
Dashboard stats that update live
watchOut: Use tabular numbers so the width does not jump
Do not animate numbers that change many times a second

items.name: avatar-stack
items.title: Avatar Stack
items.description: Overlapping avatars with image or deterministic initials fallback, a max visible count with a +N overflow chip, three sizes, optional ring color and presence dots, where hover or focus lifts an avatar and shows its name. Rendered as a labelled list with named avatars so screen readers hear every member; reduced motion keeps avatars still and fades tooltips instantly.

whenToUse: Showing collaborators on a document, project or channel
Compact team rows in cards and table cells
watchOut: Each avatar is a tab stop so tooltips work by keyboard; keep max low in dense tables
Initials colors come from the name, so two people with the same name share a color

items.name: checkin-streak
items.title: Check-in Streak
items.description: A seven-day check-in card showing done, missed, today and upcoming days with their point rewards, a streak count and a points total. Checking in calls an async onCheckIn with checking and retry states, then presses a vermilion stamp into today's circle. The reward is announced via aria-live, and under reduced motion the stamp appears instantly.

whenToUse: Daily login rewards in shop apps and member centers
Loyalty programs that pay points for coming back
watchOut: Compute todayIndex and checked days on the server in the shopper's time zone
Make onCheckIn idempotent so a double tap does not grant points twice

items.name: checkout-steps
items.title: Checkout Steps
items.description: A checkout progress indicator built on a semantic ordered list: completed steps draw a check and can jump back when onStepClick is given, the current step carries aria-current="step", and connectors fill with the theme primary as steps complete. Below the sm breakpoint it collapses to a single 'Step 2 of 4' row with a segmented bar; with reduced motion the fills and checks switch instantly.

whenToUse: Multi page or multi section checkout flows
Any short linear wizard where users may go back to edit an earlier step
watchOut: Keep it to five steps or fewer so labels fit on one row
Only let users jump back to completed steps, never skip ahead

items.name: cjk-heading
items.title: CJK Heading
items.description: Headline for Traditional Chinese and Japanese with optional vertical writing (vertical-rl with tate-chu-yoko digits), punctuation compression via text-spacing-trim with palt/halt font-feature fallbacks, automatic thin spacing between CJK and Latin text, and a staggered per-character blur-in that keeps native line breaking rules. Screen readers read the original text; reduced motion uses an instant fade.

whenToUse: Chinese or Japanese headlines on landing pages
Editorial layouts that want vertical writing
watchOut: Vertical writing needs a fixed height and short lines
Check punctuation placement in every target font

items.name: copy-code-button
items.title: Copy Code Button
items.description: A dashed coupon chip that copies a promo code to the clipboard, morphs its icon into a check and pops a Copied toast. Keyboard operable, announces success or failure via aria-live, keeps the code selectable as a fallback, and drops motion when reduced motion is preferred.

whenToUse: Coupon and promo codes in checkout or emails
Any short string the user needs to paste elsewhere
watchOut: Clipboard access needs a secure context (https or localhost)
Keep the code visible as text so it can still be copied by hand

items.name: countdown-banner
items.title: Countdown Banner
items.description: A limited-time offer banner with a live countdown, price drop and a glowing call to action.

whenToUse: Time limited sales with a real end time
Launch day announcements
watchOut: Only show a countdown that reflects a real deadline
Render the end time on the server so every visitor sees the same clock

items.name: expanding-search
items.title: Expanding Search
items.description: A search icon button that grows into a field with autofocus, a clear button and an optional suggestions dropdown, collapsing on Escape or when it loses focus while empty. The dropdown follows the ARIA combobox pattern with arrow, Home/End and Enter keys, an opt-in "/" shortcut ignores typing elsewhere, and the width animation is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Compact navbars where a full search field does not fit
Sites where search is secondary but should stay one click away
watchOut: Leave room in the layout for the expanded width so neighbouring items do not jump
Built-in filtering is a simple substring match; set filterSuggestions to false for server results

items.name: favorite-button
items.title: Favorite Button
items.description: A heart toggle for wishlists with a burst ring, small particles and an optional rolling count. Uses aria-pressed with descriptive labels, works controlled or uncontrolled, and skips the burst and bounce under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Wishlists, likes and saves on product or content cards
Lightweight toggles that deserve a little delight
watchOut: Update the count optimistically and roll back on error
Give it an accessible name that includes the item

items.name: hold-to-redeem
items.title: Hold To Redeem
items.description: A press-and-hold button for irreversible spends such as redeeming points: a fill grows linearly while held (pointer or Space/Enter), rewinds with a hint if released early, then calls an async onConfirm and turns into a paper voucher line with a vermilion Redeemed stamp and optional code. The hold instruction is wired through aria-describedby and the result is announced via aria-live; under reduced motion the rewind and stamp are instant while the time-based fill still shows progress.

whenToUse: Redeeming points, vouchers or one-time rewards that can't be undone
Any spend where an accidental tap would cost the shopper something
watchOut: Keep holdMs around one second; longer holds feel broken, not safe
Use it only for irreversible actions, or it becomes friction on ordinary buttons

items.name: low-stock-indicator
items.title: Low Stock Indicator
items.description: An honest scarcity indicator that shows the real remaining stock with a ticking count and a draining meter, shifting from emerald to amber to rose at configurable thresholds. It never fakes a countdown; changes are announced via role=status, and reduced motion removes the pulse and animation.

whenToUse: Product pages where stock is genuinely limited
Ticket and seat selection
watchOut: Only show real inventory numbers, fake scarcity erodes trust
Hide it entirely when stock is comfortable

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.description: One-time code input with N cells, auto-advance, backspace to previous cell, paste that fills every cell, numeric inputMode and autocomplete="one-time-code" for SMS autofill. Shows success and error states (error shakes the row); each cell is labelled, arrow/Home/End keys navigate, and the shake is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Sign in and two step verification codes
Short numeric codes from SMS or email
watchOut: Keep autocomplete one-time-code so phones can autofill
Do not auto-submit before the last digit is entered

items.name: payment-status-banner
items.title: Payment Status Banner
items.description: A paper receipt banner for the page shoppers land on after an external payment redirect. While pending it polls a check() function on an interval, pausing while the tab is hidden, then turns paid with a vermilion stamp, failed with a retry, or an honest timeout with a Check again button. Status changes are announced via aria-live, and under reduced motion the stamp and text swaps are instant.

whenToUse: Order confirmation pages after Stripe, PayPal or bank redirects
Any purchase where the webhook can arrive after the shopper returns
watchOut: check() should read your own order record, not trust URL query params
Keep the timeout copy honest so shoppers do not pay twice

items.name: quantity-stepper
items.title: Quantity Stepper
items.description: A minus, number and plus control for carts with min, max and step, long-press to repeat with acceleration, direct typing clamped on blur, a rolling number animation and an optional trash button at the minimum. Exposes ARIA spinbutton semantics (ArrowUp/Down, PageUp/Down, Home/End) with a polite live region, and the roll animation is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Cart and checkout line items
Any bounded numeric input changed in small steps
watchOut: The plus and minus buttons are removed from the tab order; keyboard users adjust via the field itself
Typed values snap to the nearest step, so tell users when step is larger than 1

items.name: redeem-key-input
items.title: Redeem Key Input
items.description: A printed-voucher card for redeeming gift cards, license keys and promo codes: the mono input uppercases, strips stray characters and groups the code with dashes as you type or paste, optionally detects the key type, and shows server errors inline. On success the field becomes the printed code with a vermilion Redeemed stamp; results are announced via aria-live and the stamp appears instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Account pages where customers redeem gift cards or store credit
Activating a license or supporter key in an app
watchOut: Throw an Error with an actionable message from onRedeem; the message is shown as is
Match length and groupSize to your real code format or valid codes cannot be completed

items.name: reservation-timer
items.title: Reservation Timer
items.description: A paper slip that shows how long a limited item or ticket is held for you, with a mono countdown, a hairline bar for the remaining hold and a slot for the item summary. It renders a placeholder until mounted, resyncs with real time when the tab returns, turns vermilion inside the warning window, and on expiry calls onExpire, fades and presses an ink Released stamp with an optional Hold again action. Screen readers hear only the warning crossing and the expiry, and reduced motion skips the stamp animation.

whenToUse: Ticket, seat or limited drop checkouts that hold stock for a few minutes
Cart sidebars where an item is reserved until payment
watchOut: Only show a hold the server actually enforces; never fake urgency
Release the stock on the server too, the onExpire callback is only the UI side

items.name: scroll-progress
items.title: Scroll Progress
items.description: Reading progress bar tied to the window or any scroll container, with optional section markers that show progress and jump to each section on click. Exposes a progressbar role with percent values, markers are keyboard-focusable buttons, and smoothing and smooth scrolling are turned off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Long articles, docs and changelogs
Step based onboarding pages
watchOut: Hide it on short pages where it adds noise
Section markers need stable heading ids

items.name: scroll-reveal-text
items.title: Scroll Reveal Text
items.description: A paragraph whose words light up one by one as it scrolls through the viewport or a scroll container, splitting per character for Chinese, Japanese and Korean and per word for Latin text, with optional accent words. Screen readers get the full text once; under reduced motion the text is shown fully lit.

whenToUse: Manifesto or mission statements on landing pages
Story style product sections
watchOut: Keep the full text readable without scrolling for screen readers
Long paragraphs feel slow, use it on two to four lines

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented Control
items.description: Joined segments with a pill that springs to the selected option, supporting sm, md and lg sizes, optional icons or icon-only mode, and controlled or uncontrolled use. Built as a radiogroup with roving tabindex and arrow, Home and End keys; reduced motion moves the pill instantly.

whenToUse: Switching between 2 to 5 mutually exclusive views or ranges
Compact filters like Daily, Weekly, Monthly or list and grid view
watchOut: Too many or long labels overflow; use tabs or a select instead
Icon-only options need a string label or ariaLabel for screen readers

items.name: settlement-receipt
items.title: Settlement Receipt
items.description: A torn-edge paper receipt for split bills: per-person subtotals with a line breakdown and payer tag, a balance check against the bill total, and a transfer list where each row is a checkbox to mark as sent. When every transfer is ticked a vermilion Settled stamp presses on, and a Copy summary button copies a plain-text recap. Settling is announced via aria-live and the stamp is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Bill splitting and group order results
Showing who owes whom after a shared purchase
watchOut: Pass the real bill total so mismatches surface instead of hiding rounding errors
Transfers reference people by id; unknown ids fall back to the raw id

items.name: side-panel
items.title: Side Panel
items.description: A modal drawer that slides in from the left, right or bottom with a title, description, scrollable body and sticky footer. Traps focus, closes on Escape or overlay click, locks page scroll and restores focus to the trigger; it fades instead of sliding under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Filters, carts and detail views beside a list
Mobile navigation and settings
watchOut: Trap focus and restore it to the trigger on close
Avoid stacking more than one drawer

items.name: skeleton-set
items.title: Skeleton Set
items.description: Skeleton loading primitives (line, circle, text, card, product card, list) with wave, pulse or no shimmer, plus a SkeletonSet wrapper that crossfades from the placeholder to real content when loaded. The region sets aria-busy and announces loading state via a visually hidden status; shimmer is disabled under reduced motion.

whenToUse: First load of cards, lists and profiles
Any content that takes over 300 ms to arrive
watchOut: Match the real layout so the page does not jump
Use a spinner instead for actions under a second

items.name: star-rating
items.title: Star Rating
items.description: Rating input with hover preview, optional half stars, a word label under the stars, custom icons and an emoji mood variant whose chosen face scales up, plus a read-only mode with fractional fill for averages like 4.3. Uses radiogroup semantics with arrow, Home/End and Delete keys; under reduced motion the pop and scale effects are skipped.

whenToUse: Collecting product or order reviews
Showing an average rating next to a review count
watchOut: Half-star hit areas are small on mobile; use precision 1 on touch-first forms
Pass a name prop if the value must be submitted with a native form

items.name: toast-stack
items.title: Toast Stack
items.description: Stacked notifications that fan out on hover or keyboard focus, dismiss by swipe, close button or Escape, and auto-dismiss with timers that pause while hovered or focused. Ships a useToasts hook; toasts render in a labelled region with an aria-live polite list, and springs become instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Confirmations after save, copy or add to cart
Non blocking errors that the user can retry
watchOut: Do not put critical errors only in a toast
Keep messages short and give actions a clear label

items.name: typewriter
items.title: Typewriter
items.description: Typing and deleting rotating phrases with a blinking caret (bar, block or underscore), grapheme-accurate via Intl.Segmenter and CJK-aware pacing with longer pauses after punctuation; starts when scrolled into view. Screen readers get the full text once from a visually hidden copy (aria-live off), and reduced motion swaps whole phrases without typing.

whenToUse: Hero headlines that rotate through use cases
Terminal or chat style intros
watchOut: Keep the static part of the sentence meaningful on its own
Respect reduced motion by showing the first phrase

items.name: undo-toast
items.title: Undo Toast
items.description: Replaces confirm dialogs with undo: a useUndo hook keeps one pending action and commits the previous one when a new one starts, and UndoToast shows a paper slip with an Undo button and a hairline that runs out over the duration, then commits. The timer pauses on hover, focus or when the tab is hidden; Escape commits, Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes (except while typing in a field), and the slip lives in an aria-live polite status region with instant transitions under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Removing cart items, saved addresses or wishlist entries without a confirm dialog
Any destructive action you can hold back for a few seconds before committing
watchOut: Apply the change optimistically in the UI and only call the server in onCommit
Don't use it for actions that can't be held back, such as payments
